title: [C#] ScriptPathAttributeGenerator throws for projects depending on the main project, interfering with Rider auto-refactor features
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in v4.6.0-4.6.1 stable.

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.8247) - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 285HX (24 threads) - 63.45 GiB memory

### Issue description

#### Summary

If a secondary C# project, such as a unit test project, depends on the main C# project linked to Godot, the `GodotProjectDir` is null in `ScriptPathAttributeGenerator`, throwing an exception. This happens when using the Jetbrains Rider's function to auto-adjust namespaces, causing it to fail on either project.

#### Expected

If possible, either `GodotProjectDir` should be propagated to all secondary C# projects or `ScriptPathAttributeGenerator` should never run for secondary C# projects.

#### File at fault

[ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs, lines 25-29](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Godot project
2. Create a C# solution for the Godot project
3. Create/add a second C# project to the solution
4. Set the first project as a dependency for the second, either via the .sln or by a <ProjectReference> in the .csproj
5. Open the project in Rider
6. Create a .cs file with the wrong namepsace
7. Try to use the Rider auto-adjust namespace context action
